rows.question: In Team IS1000, which speaker championed keeping an LCD screen and on what grounds, and what happened to the LCD and to speech recognition in the final costing?

rows.question: Trace Team ES2012's voice-recognition idea: who first floated a remote with no buttons using voice recognition, what risk did the designer raise in the next meeting, and was voice control in the final design?
rows.ground_truth: Speaker A floated a remote with no buttons at all via voice recognition (ES2012b). In ES2012c Speaker B warned the voice technology was not highly developed / still experimental; A nonetheless confirmed it will have voice recognition. In ES2012d the final remote has a microphone for voice commands (and a speech 'where are you' function), alongside a few buttons.
rows.answer: Speaker A (Project Manager) first floated a remote control with no buttons using voice recognition in meeting b. In the next meeting (meeting c), the Industrial Designer raised the risk that the voice technology was still in an experimental form and not well developed. Voice control was included in the final design as part of a dual-function setup alongside essential physical buttons.
